items.title: Faster memory access in game code
items.text: Loads and stores in recompiled game code now take fewer CPU instructions, so games run a bit faster.

items.title: Faster math in game code
items.text: Multiplies and divides by constant numbers, multiply-add steps and pairs of shifts now compile to fewer, cheaper instructions, so games run a bit faster.

items.title: Fewer wasted interrupt checks
items.text: After certain CPU status changes, an interrupt check is now scheduled only when it could actually do something, which removes needless work.

items.title: Layouts stay put under the keyboard
items.text: The game library, the pad layout editor and the menus no longer switch between portrait and landscape layouts when an on-screen keyboard shrinks the window. This matters most on iPhone Duo's short portrait screens.

items.title: Focus ring and VoiceOver fixes
items.text: In right-to-left languages such as Arabic, the controller focus ring is no longer drawn mirrored away from the control it belongs to. There are also small VoiceOver and layout fixes for every device.

items.title: iPhone Duo fold and hinge support
items.text: The app now reads the hinge and fold of iPhone Duo, and the pause card and in-game panels lay themselves out around the fold. Folding or unfolding with the pause card open keeps the item a controller had selected instead of jumping back to Resume.

items.title: Pad and OrbitKeys fit iPhone Duo
items.text: The built-in on-screen pad is refit to iPhone Duo's shorter portrait screens. OrbitKeys now sizes its keys and keyboard space by window size, so the inner screen no longer gets phone-sized keys.

items.title: More accurate CPU instruction timing
items.text: The cost of divides, square roots and many other CPU instructions now matches timings measured on a real console, so game timing is closer to the original.

items.title: Haptic Feedback toggle takes effect at once
items.text: Turning Haptic Feedback off in the middle of a game now stops the phone rumble right away. Before, the fallback kept tapping until the next game.

items.title: Remove Disc Link works again
items.text: The disc link panel can clear a linked disc again. Before, a linked disc could be changed but never removed.

items.title: Turbo and slow motion speeds apply as saved
items.text: Turbo and slow motion speeds now go live exactly as you saved them. Before, they were squeezed into a 0.05 to 10 range while running, so the live speed and the saved value disagreed.

items.title: Fixes for rare crashes and glitches
items.text: Fixed rare out-of-range memory reads and writes in USB microphone setup, in-game video decoding and texture pack loading. Also fixed a buffer wrap bug in multithreaded VU mode and two ARM64 low-level setup mistakes.

items.title: Safer audio buffer handoff
items.text: Fixed a rare timing problem between the emulation and audio threads in the shared sound buffer.

items.title: Audio stretching moves to its own thread
items.text: Time stretching and surround expansion of the sound now run on a worker thread, with faster vector maths on ARM64, which takes load off the emulation thread. Stopping a sound stream also no longer waits for queued audio.

items.title: Faster sound mixing
items.text: The sound chip mixer does less work for every voice and every sample, and uses the CPU's vector instructions for voice interpolation and reverb, so games spend less time on audio.

items.title: Faster I/O processor code
items.text: Code that runs on the console's I/O processor is recompiled more efficiently: RAM loads are inlined, its clocks stay in CPU registers and less is saved on entry. Games run faster.

items.title: Fix stray audio in bypass mode
items.text: Fixed a stray leftover value that leaked into the audio of games that put the sound chip in bypass mode.

items.title: Fix a stale CPU sprite decision
items.text: Fixed a wrong decision about drawing sprites on the CPU that used leftover state from the previous draw.

items.title: More precise texture cache tracking
items.text: The texture cache now tracks changed areas of a target one block at a time, so a CPU write marks only the blocks it touched.

items.title: Cheaper CPU sprite copy draws
items.text: Copy-style draws done on the CPU now read textures and write the frame a block at a time, which makes them cheaper.

items.title: Faster software renderer colour tables
items.text: The software renderer now builds only the colour and fog table entry each row needs, so it does less work per row.

items.title: Cheaper vertex handling for sprite pairs
items.text: Sprite pairs now take the fast vertex path, including with autoflush on, and a draw's settings are copied once instead of four times when draw buffering is off. The graphics thread uses less CPU.

items.title: Clearer BIOS errors and checks
items.text: A boot with a BIOS that is missing, unreadable, empty or not a PS2 BIOS now says which problem it is, instead of always asking for a BIOS. A PlayStation 1 BIOS, such as one copied from a PS3, is named as one and skipped by the BIOS search.

items.title: Recompiler stops with the right error
items.text: When a game jumps to an unmapped or misaligned address, the recompilers now stop with an accurate error instead of dispatching a wrongly looked-up block.

items.title: VSync mode kept when graphics restart
items.text: When the graphics device restarts, it now keeps the VSync mode you asked for instead of one the old device had fallen back to.

items.title: Faster 8-bit palette textures
items.text: 8-bit palette textures now expand with integer lookups instead of moving every pixel through vector lanes, which is faster on ARM64.
